licence_note: HPWREN imagery carries no SPDX licence and requires a credit reference. These windows contain no fire and are used ONLY as the false-alarm denominator that rank.solve_threshold is calibrated on.
url_note: Frame URL = window url_prefix + frame, with '+' percent-encoded as %2B. A frame name carries its own quarter directory because an 81-minute window can straddle two of them. The file name is a UTC epoch but the directory is San Diego local: the date is the local date and Q<n> is the local three-hour block numbered from 1 at local midnight, so n runs 1..8. Probed hour by hour against the live bucket; spike/urls_fog.txt alone cannot pin this, because all 60 of its URLs fall in the one band where a UTC six-hour reading gives the same answer.
catalogue: The MTA publishes no directory index (the bucket answers AccessDenied to a bare directory, to ?list-type=2 and to index.html), so frames were enumerated by probing the 60 s grid with a +/-3 s jitter search.
selection: Every window is on a camera that appears in manifest_hold.json and is centred within +/-45 min of the local time of day of that camera's paired HOLD ignition. A confusion set on other cameras or at another hour would be a straw man; tests/test_confusion_set.py and test_confuse_shares_cameras assert both from the frame epochs rather than from these fields.
One window per camera, so the denominator spans the roster instead of concentrating on whichever camera happened to be foggiest.

Within each class, candidates were ranked by raw S3 -- PlumeRank's own fog discriminator -- and each class offers its cameras hardest-first. The arm is adversarial to this project by construction, which makes the solved threshold conservative. Read that as a PREFERENCE and not a guarantee: see the next point.

Cameras were assigned to class slots by a maximum-cardinality matching (Kuhn's augmenting paths), not by walking the classes in some order and taking each one's hardest unused camera. Cardinality is what is optimised exactly, so a class that comes up short is short on SUPPLY -- no assignment of these cameras to these slots fills more -- and the shortfall is a statement about the corpus rather than about the walk order. Hardness enters only as the order in which each class offers its cameras and as the scarcest-supply order in which slots are offered, which decides WHICH maximum matching is found when several exist. So an individual window is not guaranteed to be the hardest candidate its class had: the matching may displace a harder camera onto another of its own classes in order to fill one more slot. Where a shortfall record shows selected == cameras_measured_in_this_class, that class took every camera that could supply it and no hardness was traded away inside it.

A selected window the archive could not deliver as 81 consecutive minutes was dropped and its class re-filled from the next-hardest candidate, never shortened. Every such rejection is listed under incomplete_enumerations, so the rows the CDN decided are separable from the rows the predicate decided.

The fog predicate was CALIBRATED on this project's own labelled fog -- the 60 frames in spike/urls_fog.txt that a human picked and visually confirmed as marine layer -- against a camera- and clock-matched background sample drawn from the same six cameras on other days. The statistic that separates them is deck_fraction and the cutline is the median of the labelled class. The previous revision's a priori cutlines (edge_energy <= 18.0, sky_ground_ratio <= 1.05) were re-measured on that same labelled set, admitted zero of 60, and were discarded rather than moved. The full record, including the discarded statistics and the background frames, is under 'calibration'.

A predicate calibrated on 60 frames from 6 cameras is a screening rule and not a fog detector, and this arm is an adversary set and not a ground truth. No window here is certified as fog; the class labels say which predicate admitted the window, and the measured features say on what evidence.

Non-fire basis: candidate days exclude every (camera, date) FIgLib records a fire on, and every window additionally had to satisfy one of the six confuser predicates. FIgLib catalogues 521 fires and not every fire, so this is a filter and not a certification.

clock_note.note: Every window here is within +/-45 min of its camera's paired HOLD ignition, which is what stops the arm being a straw man -- and it is also the hardest constraint on the fog class. Fires ignite in the afternoon, so that is the hour HOLD fixes; coastal marine layer is a DAWN object, and it is the hour the labelled set in spike/urls_fog.txt was drawn from. The two counts above are how far apart those hours are. Read the fog_marine class accordingly: outside the early-morning windows it is not dawn marine layer, it is whatever satisfies a deck predicate calibrated on dawn marine layer at an hour marine layer has usually burnt off -- a bright, textureless surface lying where terrain belongs. That is a legitimate adversary for S3, which is what this arm is for, and it is NOT evidence about fog. Matching the clock and calling the class fog were always going to be in tension; the tension is published rather than resolved by quietly relaxing one of them.

class_precedence_note.note: classify() evaluates the six predicates in class_order, so 'satisfies the fog_marine predicate' means 'deck_fraction >= FOG_DECK_FRACTION_MIN AND no earlier class fired'. A reader who screens these rows on deck_fraction alone will therefore count MORE windows above the cutline than the fog_marine histogram shows, and the count above is exactly that difference, listed per class. The order is a priori and documented on _CLASS_ORDER -- a camera with a hunting shutter or a droplet on the glass is that, whatever the weather behind it is doing -- and it was NOT chosen to move windows between classes. It is recorded here because reordering it is the one remaining lever that could refill the fog class without touching a cutline, and a reader is entitled to see the size of that lever rather than discover it.

shortfalls.reason: The sweep measured 2 candidate windows that satisfy the 'dust' predicate, on 1 distinct cameras, and one window is taken per camera. 1 slots were filled, and that is the MAXIMUM over every assignment of these cameras to these slots -- no ordering fills more, so the deficit is the archive's and not the selector's. The class was reduced. The predicate was NOT moved: see criterion_thresholds and calibration.

The sweep measured 24 candidate windows that satisfy the 'fog_marine' predicate, on 13 distinct cameras, and one window is taken per camera. 13 slots were filled, and that is the MAXIMUM over every assignment of these cameras to these slots -- no ordering fills more, so the deficit is the archive's and not the selector's. The class was reduced. The predicate was NOT moved: see criterion_thresholds and calibration.

incomplete_enumerations.reason: The archive does not hold every minute of this window. It was dropped and its class re-filled from the next-hardest candidate; the window was NOT shortened and no threshold was moved.

incomplete_enumerations_note: Windows the predicate selected and the ARCHIVE could not deliver whole. A window is 81 consecutive minutes or it is not a window, so each of these was dropped and its class re-filled from the next-hardest candidate in the same ranked pool. They are listed because the alternative -- silently taking the second choice -- would make the selection unre-derivable from the record. Distinct from shortfalls, which is a class the CORPUS could not fill.
composition_note: class_quotas is what was asked for and class_histogram is what the archive supplied. Where they differ, shortfalls carries the class, the deficit and the reason, and the reason is never a moved threshold: a class the sweep could not fill was REDUCED. Quote n_windows and class_histogram, never class_quotas.

provenance.FOG_DECK_FRACTION_MIN: CALIBRATED on the 60 hand-labelled marine-layer frames in spike/urls_fog.txt -- the median of that class. See calibration.
provenance.LOW_CLOUD_SKY_GREYNESS_MIN: CALIBRATED the same way, on the same labelled class, which is marine layer and not low cloud. See calibration.low_cloud_note.
provenance.everything_else: a priori. Chosen from the physics of each process, never fitted, and never moved to make a quota fall out. Of these, the lens_artefact and cloud_shadow cutlines have no labelled set behind them at all and are the weakest claims in this file.

rules.lens_artefact: sky_novel_structure >= 0.02 (fraction of sky pixels with mean gradient >= 12.0 and temporal std <= 2.0 in THIS window, and not in this camera's cross-day furniture reference)
rules.fog_marine: deck_fraction >= 0.12847 -- CALIBRATED as the median of the 60 hand-labelled marine-layer frames in spike/urls_fog.txt
rules.low_cloud: deck_fraction < 0.12847 and sky_greyness >= -0.1314 -- the grey-ceiling residual of the calibrated fog test; see calibration.low_cloud_note

positive_class.label: hand-picked and visually confirmed as marine-layer fog by a human before this file existed. It is the only labelled fog in the project.

background_class.rule: For each labelled fog frame, one frame from the SAME camera at the SAME local minute of day on a different day, day offsets tried in the order [-35, -28, -21, -14, -7, 7, 14, 21, 28, 35, -42, -49, 42, -56, -63] rotated by the frame's index modulo 10, skipping any day that camera has a labelled fog frame on.
background_class.not_a_negative_class: This sample is UNLABELLED. It is the population the candidate sweep draws from, at dawn on coastal ridge cameras in June to August, and a large share of it is genuinely foggy. Every AUC below is therefore a LOWER bound on the statistic's separation, not an estimate of it.

calibration.cutline_rule: Each cutline is the MEDIAN of the labelled fog class for that statistic -- fixed as a rule before the values were read, so that no cutline could be walked until a class quota fell out.

discarded.edge_energy: The previous revision's fog test, at edge_energy <= 18.0. Not one of the 60 labelled fog frames reaches it. It does carry some signal in the opposite bookkeeping -- AUC 0.386, which is 0.614 with fog as the lower class -- but it is whole-frame, so on these cameras it is dominated by near-field terrain that a marine layer never touches, and no cutline reachable by the labelled set is reachable by anything else either. Discarded, not retuned.
discarded.sky_ground_ratio: The previous revision's fog/low-cloud split, at <= 1.05. The a priori claim was that a marine layer lifts the ground to the sky's brightness. These are ridge-top cameras looking DOWN on the layer: the sky is the bright thing and the near foreground under the deck is the dark thing, on a clear morning as much as a foggy one, and the labelled set never falls below 1.46. Worse than unreachable, the sign is inverted: fog measures HIGHER than the background sample (AUC 0.604), so the published rule was not merely tight, it pointed the wrong way. Discarded.
discarded.sky_smooth_fraction: Tried by this revision as a low-cloud ceiling detector and thrown away: a clear sky is smooth too. AUC 0.488, 95% CI [0.385, 0.599] -- the interval spans 0.5, so this statistic is not measured to separate anything and no cutline was taken from it.

calibration.internal_parameter_note: DECK_LUMA_FRACTION=0.35 and DECK_TEXTURE_FRACTION=0.08 were chosen from a 20-point grid on this same labelled sample, so the deck AUC is in-sample and optimistic. Neighbouring grid points span roughly 0.65-0.71, which is the size of that optimism.
calibration.low_cloud_note: low_cloud has NO labelled set anywhere in this project. Its cutline is the median sky greyness of the MARINE-LAYER class, and the class is defined as the residual: a sky as grey as a median marine-layer morning, with no bright deck under the horizon. That is a defensible construction and it is not a measurement of low cloud.
calibration.limitation: A predicate calibrated on 60 frames from 6 cameras is a SCREENING RULE, not a fog detector, and the CONFUSE arm is an adversary set, not a ground truth. It is applied to 45 cameras, 39 of which contributed nothing to the calibration. Per-camera AUC on the six that did ranges from 0.28 to 0.86, so the rule does not transfer evenly even inside its own calibration set. Nothing downstream may describe a window in this arm as verified fog; what the arm supports is the statement that rank.solve_threshold was calibrated on non-fire windows enriched for fog, on the evaluation cameras, at the evaluation hour.

sha256_note: Per-file sha256 is not in this manifest and that is deliberate: hashing the frames requires downloading them, which is what scripts/fetch.py does. It writes data/fetch_receipt.json on the first fetch and verifies against it on every later run. The manifest pins WHICH frames; the receipt pins WHAT they contained.
